articles.title: Install ESP firmware from an Android phone
articles.dek: ESP Web Tools adds USB support in Chrome on Android, including boards with common serial bridge chips.
body: ESP Web Tools brings USB firmware installation to Chrome on Android. Makers can connect a supported ESP device to a phone or tablet through a USB-C cable or USB OTG adapter, without installing desktop drivers. Chrome’s native serial picker on Android previously listed Bluetooth devices rather than these USB boards.

Jesse Hills adds support for native USB devices and the CP210x, CH340/CH341 and FTDI serial bridges used by many ESP boards. Complete installations were tested on a Pixel through CP2102, CH340 and FTDI connections at 115,200 baud; faster transfers were not tested.

The logs view fills a phone’s screen and stays above the on-screen keyboard, keeping its command field and controls reachable. During installation, the tool requests a screen wake lock where supported to reduce interruptions when the display would otherwise sleep.

pullRequests.title: Use web-serial-polyfill on Android Chrome
Add WebUSB drivers for CP210x, CH340/341 and FTDI
Mention Android Chrome support
Make the logs view fill the screen on phones
Hold a screen wake lock while installing

articles.title: Older wall displays can try Home Assistant again
articles.dek: A Continue anyway button replaces the hard stop below the supported browser minimums.
body: Home Assistant lets people with older wall displays continue past the unsupported-browser warning. The browser minimums introduced in October had stopped these devices at the launch screen, even where much of a dashboard still worked.

The first visit offers Continue anyway. The warning returns monthly, then also offers Don’t show again; the choice is saved on that device and cleared by logging out. This is an override, not a promise of compatibility. The change was tested in Chromium 66.

pullRequests.title: Let browsers below the legacy floor continue at their own risk

articles.title: Git pull keeps Home Assistant’s configuration when a download fails
articles.dek: The app fetches a replacement successfully before touching the existing files.
body: Home Assistant’s Git pull app stops deleting the existing configuration before it knows the replacement repository can be downloaded. An unreachable repository or missing credentials previously left the configuration lost, with its only backup in temporary storage that would disappear on a container restart.

The app clones into a temporary directory first and changes the configuration only after that succeeds. It also avoids setting up an SSH key for repositories accessed through HTTPS. The existing restoration of secrets and other non-YAML files remains in place.

pullRequests.title: git_pull: Do not wipe /config when the clone fails
git_pull: Only use deployment_key for SSH repositories

articles.title: Music Assistant tunes into Apple Music’s live stations
articles.dek: Apple Music 1 and Club join the radio browser, with the current song’s details carried alongside the broadcast.
body: Music Assistant adds playback of Apple Music’s live radio stations, including Apple Music 1 and Apple Music Club. They appear in radio browsing and search, bringing broadcasts that were previously skipped into the Apple Music provider.

Listening requires a paid Apple Music subscription and the same account and decryption setup used for songs. The stream supplies the current track’s title, artist, album and artwork. The provider allows one concurrent stream per account, so a station occupies that account’s listening slot.

pullRequests.title: Play the live Apple Music radio stations

articles.title: MariaDB backups wait until the database is actually locked
articles.dek: A busy database could previously be copied while it was still accepting writes.
body: Home Assistant’s MariaDB app waits for its database backup lock to be acquired before letting Supervisor copy the files. Previously it reported success as soon as it requested the lock, even when a long-running operation still prevented that lock from taking effect.

The request times out after thirty seconds. If it cannot acquire the lock, the backup completes without the MariaDB app and records the failed preparation step, rather than including an unlocked copy. Tests on a Home Assistant OS installation confirmed that waiting writes resume after a failed attempt and a later backup can acquire the lock again.

pullRequests.title: Wait until the backup lock is held before reporting it

articles.title: Matter.js hides network secrets in ordinary logs
articles.dek: The library redacts credentials and pairing secrets, while raw debug payloads still need separate protection.
body: Matter.js removes marked secret fields from its normal command, attribute and diagnostic logs. Those messages could previously include Wi-Fi credentials, Thread network keys and pairing secrets, exposing them when someone shared a log for troubleshooting.

Ingo Fischer’s correction marks forty-one standard fields for redaction on controller and device paths. It changes logging rather than the messages sent to devices. Applications using Matter.js need to adopt the library change.

This does not make every debug log safe to share. Raw decrypted message payloads remain enabled by default and can contain the same secrets; applications can disable those payload logs separately. Values embedded in error messages and unmarked custom-cluster fields are also outside this correction.

pullRequests.title: fix: redact secret fields in log output

articles.title: History graphs stop drawing changes that did not happen
articles.dek: Long periods without a state change stay flat instead of curving toward the next reading.
body: Home Assistant’s history graphs hold a sensor’s last value across long gaps between recorded changes. A fan that stayed off all night could previously look as though it gradually ramped up, because the line curved toward the next value before that change happened.

The correction preserves the flat stretch through graph sampling and keeps the transition near the recorded change. An unavailable reading does not create a hold, and forecasts and histories without a sufficiently long gap keep their existing curves.

pullRequests.title: Hold the last value across gaps in history graphs

media.alt: Before-and-after history graphs comparing curved transitions with flat holds across unchanged readings

articles.title: Home Assistant points automation errors at the field that needs fixing
articles.dek: Related validation changes replace misleading paths and generic failures with precise locations.
body: Home Assistant makes invalid automation and script messages point to the configuration as it was written. Errors in nested conditions, parallel actions, triggers and templates identify the failing field rather than a parent block or an extra list position that does not exist.

An unfinished device action reports the empty device field, and an invalid entity name is identified as such instead of suggesting that it must be “all” or “none”. The more precise paths also appear in configuration validation responses, logs and repair notices, making complex configurations easier to correct.

articles.title: Music Assistant brings party hosting into its mobile app
articles.dek: A native panel shows the guest QR code and gives hosts control over invitations and party settings.
body: Music Assistant’s mobile app adds a Party panel when the optional Party plugin is loaded for the person hosting a shared listening session. It displays the guest QR code and a copyable invitation link, with the party name and invitation text supplied by the server.

People with permission to configure the Party plugin can switch guest access on or off and edit settings such as the speaker, party name and duration in the same panel. Guests still join through the web interface; this change brings the host’s controls into the app.

articles.title: KNX setup suggestions reach sensors, meters and fans
articles.dek: Home Assistant reads more of an imported ETS project to prepare entity configurations.
body: Home Assistant expands its KNX configuration suggestions beyond lighting and covers to sensors, meters, fans and general-purpose inputs and outputs. The suggestions use the imported ETS project’s descriptions of device functions and addresses, reducing the address matching needed to set up these entities.

Coverage includes temperature, air quality, humidity and brightness sensors; window, presence and weather-alarm signals; fan speed; and energy or volume readings from meters. Suggestions do not create entities automatically. Sensor units and classifications still need setting, and the meter suggestions cover consumption rather than every power, flow or temperature reading.

articles.title: Computer notification buttons can answer Home Assistant automations
articles.dek: System Bridge links each notification to its click and close events, including supported paired phones.
body: Home Assistant gives System Bridge notifications up to three labeled buttons and an identifier that automations can follow. A new event entity reports the notification being sent, clicked or closed, with the identifier and button action connecting each response to the original message.

The available events depend on the computer: Linux reports clicks and closes, Windows reports clicks, and macOS reports neither. Event support starts with System Bridge 5.20, sent events need 5.27, and version 5.28 carries the same button replies from paired Android phones.
The new notification action replaces the legacy host-specific action, which is scheduled for removal in June 2027. A repair notice provides migration examples.

articles.title: System Bridge shares a file link without sharing its API token
articles.dek: Supported computers issue a link for one file with a twenty-four-hour lifetime.
body: Home Assistant uses signed file links when sending System Bridge media to a player, keeping the computer’s full API token out of those URLs. Previously, a receiving player such as a Cast device got a URL containing that token, which could authorize other System Bridge requests.

The signed link is limited to the chosen file and expires after twenty-four hours. This requires System Bridge 5.25 or newer; older hosts keep the token-based links. Correctly encoding the file path also lets names containing spaces or ampersands work.

pullRequests.title: Sign System Bridge media file URLs instead of sending the token

articles.title: Music Assistant tightens who can control shared speakers
articles.dek: Group changes and sleep timers check speaker permissions, while owners retain a way to stop their own speaker’s group session.
body: Music Assistant applies speaker access checks to group changes, party and quiz listening, and sleep timers. Adding speakers to a group requires permission for both the target and the speakers being added, closing a gap where access to one speaker could reach others.

The changes also preserve an exit for someone whose own speaker belongs to a fixed group they cannot otherwise control. They can stop that group’s session to release their speaker; that action stops the shared session, rather than silently removing just their room.

articles.title: Home Assistant stops offering a reset for the wrong Thread network
articles.dek: A border router that moved networks no longer appears as the old network’s reset target.
body: Home Assistant checks which Thread network a border router actually belongs to before offering it as that network’s preferred router. Previously, a router moved to another network could still appear on the old network’s card with a Reset border router button.
Pressing that button would factory-reset the router and create a new network, dropping the network it was really using. Matching the router’s current network prevents that misleading reset option.

articles.title: Home Assistant takes control of compatible Shelly fans
articles.dek: Fan entities add speed and power controls alongside the device’s automatic mode.
body: Home Assistant adds a fan control for generation-two-and-later Shelly devices that expose a fan component. It can turn the fan on or off, choose its speed as a percentage, or return control to the device’s automatic mode.

Changing power or speed selects Manual mode. Switching from Auto to Manual preserves the current output until another command changes it. The accompanying guide also brings together the fan’s boost control and its humidity, light-level and energy readings; boost is available in Auto mode.

articles.title: Speech-to-Phrase gains a Slovak command grammar
articles.dek: Community phrases become part of the sentence library for constrained local speech recognition.
body: Speech-to-Phrase’s sentence library gains Slovak definitions covering 22 kinds of request. The work adapts community-contributed phrases into Home Assistant’s existing Slovak grammar, giving the recognizer a defined set of Slovak commands to work with.
Michael Hansen adapts the phrases with review by LubosKadasi. This is support in the command library; it does not by itself establish the release of a new Slovak speech model.

articles.title: ESPHome lights built with ESP-IDF can follow WLED streams
articles.dek: The WLED effect no longer requires an Arduino-based build.
body: ESPHome extends its WLED light effect to ESP32 devices built with ESP-IDF. The effect receives lighting frames over the network, allowing those lights to follow the same supported WLED streams that previously required Arduino.
J. Nick Koston extends the receiving code to ESP-IDF while retaining the supported frame formats and synchronization groups.

articles.title: Utility meters stop skipping February resets
articles.dek: An invalid day-29 setting moves to day 28; later reset dates need a custom schedule.
body: Home Assistant limits utility-meter offsets in its setup screen to twenty-seven days, making the latest resulting reset day the twenty-eighth. The old screen allowed an offset that reset a monthly meter on day twenty-nine, skipping February entirely in a non-leap year.

Existing meters with that invalid offset move to twenty-seven days automatically. Owners who need a later reset day can use a cron schedule in YAML; the normal YAML offset limit already matched the corrected screen.

pullRequests.title: Limit utility_meter config flow offset to 27 days
